# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination

**RE: Appeal of Denial — Reference Number POC-8AD74FF769-66861**
**Member:** Reese Mercado
**Member ID:** W529317483
**Plan:** Cigna (Commercial/ACA), Arizona
**Date of Denial Notice:** 2026-08-01
**Procedure:** Partial knee replacement, CPT 27446
**Governing Policy:** Cigna CMM-311 Knee Replacement/Arthroplasty V1.0.2026 (Partial Knee Replacement section), effective 2026-08-04 — https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2026-04/Cigna_CMM-311%20Knee%20Replac%20Arthro_V1.0.2026_Eff08.04.2026_Pub04.20.2026.pdf

Dear Cigna Appeals Department,

I am asking Cigna to reconsider the denial of the partial knee replacement (CPT 27446) that my surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has recommended for me. The denial notice states that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I believe my medical records show that I meet the plan's own published criteria for this surgery, and I am asking for a full review of that evidence.

## How my records match the plan's own criteria

The plan's policy states that "unicompartmental replacement is considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria have been met:"

**1. Function-limiting pain and loss of knee function.**
The policy requires "◦ function-limiting pain at short distances (e.g., walking less than one-quarter mile, limiting activity to two [2] city blocks, the equivalent to walking the length of a shopping mall) ◦ loss of knee function which interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment." My records document that I cannot climb stairs without assistance and that I wake 3–4 times nightly because of pain — both of which reflect loss of function that interferes with daily activities. [If a specific walking-distance limitation is documented elsewhere in my chart, please add it here before submitting.]

**2. Failure of at least 3 months of non-surgical management, or documentation of why it is not appropriate.**
The policy requires "Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months' duration," with a "Criteria exception" that applies when "Provider-directed non-surgical management may be inappropriate," and further states that "The medical record must clearly document why provider-directed non-surgical management is not appropriate." My records show 8 months of NSAID therapy with inadequate relief, a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-18 that gave only 3 weeks of partial relief, and supervised physical therapy from 2026-05-12 to 2026-07-07 (24 visits). Taken together, this non-surgical treatment spans well beyond the 3-month period the policy describes, without producing lasting improvement.

**3. Imaging findings.**
My MRI from 2026-06-08 shows full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition, and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 changes medially. I understand the denial reason cites imaging as insufficient, but this MRI documents advanced, isolated single-compartment degeneration — the pattern the policy's unicompartmental-replacement criteria are describing. I am asking Cigna to explain, in light of this specific finding, what additional imaging element the plan believes is missing.

I have also reviewed the policy's non-indications language, including that "Partial knee replacement (medial, lateral, or patellofemoral) is considered not medically necessary for ANY other indication, condition, or when ANY of the following are present," and that "Conservative management or surgical fixation is not considered a reasonable option" is listed among the total knee replacement criteria. Nothing in my records suggests any of the excluded conditions apply to me; my findings are isolated to the medial compartment.

## What I am asking for

I am requesting that Cigna reverse this denial and approve the partial knee replacement (CPT 27446), or, if further clarification is needed, tell me specifically what additional documentation would resolve the imaging concern so my surgeon's office can provide it promptly.

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-01-28, and I am submitting it accordingly. I understand I can submit this appeal by logging in at my.cigna.com to find my plan's appeal form, by calling 1-800-244-6224 or the number on my member ID card, or by mailing it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter.

Please let me know if any additional records or forms are needed to complete this review.

Sincerely,

[Reese Mercado]
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
Member ID: W529317483
Date: [date of submission]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
